newsitem.title: CANADA: Chretien to let provinces refund tax on books.
newsitem.headline: Chretien to let provinces refund tax on books.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien has agreed to allow provinces effectively to opt out of taxing book sales when they merge provincial and federal sales taxes, spokeswoman Leslie Swartman said on Thursday.
She was speaking from Nova Scotia, where Chretien had met with provincial Premier John Savage, who had opposed the idea of taxing books when provincial and federal taxes are blended.
Nova Scotia does not tax books but the federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) does.
"The premier (Savage) has said that he didn't want to charge the province's eight percent on books, and he said that he would refund that money to consumers," Swartman said.

"The prime minister (Chretien) spoke with him this morning, and he said that's okay by him, that the province has the flexibility to lower the tax or withdraw it on whatever items, but that the federal portion, the federal seven percent would still remain on books."

Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Newfoundland agreed this year, with the enticement of C$961 million from Ottawa to compensate for lower provincial levies, to merge their taxes with the GST to a uniform total 15 percent rate.
